full_judgment:
(1) maintainability, of the suit, limitation, suit barred under section 42 of the Specific Relief Act, res judicata and defect of parties. 

 3. Mr. Alimuzzaman Chowdhury has taken me through the order impugned. I find that the learned Assistant Judge in a very slip-shod manner failed to decide the issue on limitation which is an issue of law. Mr. Alimuzzaman placing reliance upon rule 2 of Order 14 CPC contends that the provision is mandatory and the court first is to decide the issue on limitation as it is incumbent upon the court to determine the issue of law first as it saves unnecessary expense, time and labour of the court itself. In a number of decisions of this sub-continent it has been held that when an issue of law is framed and the parties seek decision on that in a suit the court should decide that issue first In this case that has not been done. 

 Mr. AKM Abdul Wahab, however, argued to support the order of the trial Court. He made a submisssion that as the learned Judge has not decided the issue on limitation, therefore, it is pending. The contention is misconceived. Failure to decide the issue on limitation on the face of Or. 14, r.2 CPC is an error of law on the part of the Court and contrary to the decisions consistently followed by the superior courts of this sub-continent. The provision of Or. 14, r. 2 CPC, in my opinion, is mandatory and the trial Court is under mandate of law to decide the issues of law where an application under Or. 14, r. 2 CPC is filed by a party to the suit. In this view of the provision of the law I am convinced that the order impugned calls for interference by this Court.
